item.title: 2027: Yari urges Zamfara voters to back APC candidates
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau The Director-General of President Bola Tinubu’s Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has urged voters in Zamfara State to support All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates at all levels in the 2027 general elections. Yari made the appeal on Monday at the flag-off of the re-election campaign of Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, in Talata Mafara, headquarters of Talata Mafara Local Government Area. The event attracted supporters from the 14 local government areas of the state, including party faithful, women and youth groups, traditional leaders and other political stakeholders. Addressing the gathering, Yari, a former governor of Zamfara State and senator representing Zamfara West, said voting for the APC at all levels, from the presidency to the state Houses of Assembly, would enable the state to benefit from federal government projects, appointments and other interventions. He argued that Zamfara could not afford to remain in opposition in 2027, urging residents to align with the ruling party at the federal level. “I urge you, the good people of Zamfara, to vote for APC from top to bottom in 2027. Vote for President Tinubu, vote for Governor Lawal, vote for our senators, House of Representatives members and State Assembly members. That is the only way Zamfara will move forward,” Yari said. He also urged voters to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, describing the President as the candidate capable of driving development in the North-West and the country. Yari said the Tinubu administration had demonstrated commitment to addressing insecurity, reviving the economy, improving infrastructure and repositioning the country for sustainable growth. He noted that the North-West, which had experienced years of banditry, kidnapping and economic challenges, needed sustained investment in security and development. “President Tinubu is the only candidate who, if given a second mandate, will develop the North-West and the country at large. He has the vision, the experience and the political will to take Nigeria to the next level. We must give him our full support,” he said. Yari called on Zamfara residents to give Tinubu substantial electoral support in 2027, as they did in 2023, to enable him to complete his reform agenda. He also canvassed support for Governor Lawal’s second-term ambition, saying the governor needed the backing of residents to consolidate his administration’s Rescue Zamfara Agenda. According to him, cooperation between the Federal Government and the Zamfara State Government would accelerate development in security, job creation, education, healthcare and infrastructure. The campaign launch was attended by APC stakeholders, government officials, members of the state executive council, federal and state lawmakers, local government chairmen, women and youth groups, and party supporters. item.title: 2027: No alliance between Otti, Orji Kalu — LP
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The Labour Party (LP) in Abia State has denied any political alliance between Governor Alex Otti and Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, representing Abia North Senatorial District, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party also urged Kalu to desist from what it described as attempts to impose a political coalition on it, insisting that it was not interested in any alliance with the All Progressives Congress (APC) or any other party for the Abia North senatorial seat. The state Publicity Secretary of the party, Emenike Iroegbu, stated this following the dismantling of a billboard bearing the portraits of Otti and Kalu in Arochukwu Local Government Area. Iroegbu said the billboard, titled ‘Coalition of Choice’, was intended to create the impression of a political alliance between the governor and the senator, insisting that no such arrangement existed. The billboard was reportedly dismantled over concerns that it could mislead the public and for allegedly failing to comply with statutory outdoor advertising regulations. The party condemned its erection, describing it as an attempt to misinform voters in Abia North. Iroegbu said, “We have made it categorically clear that the Labour Party in Abia State is neither in talks nor in any form of political coalition with the APC or any other political party. “The Labour Party in Abia State has no coalition with any party as regards Abia North Senatorial Seat, and it is wrong for individuals or groups to erect billboards misinforming our people about a coalition when there is none. “We call on Senator Orji Uzor Kalu to stop trying to force a coalition on the Labour Party. Our party is not interested in any coalition for the Abia North senatorial seat.” He further alleged that Kalu was seeking to associate himself politically with Governor Otti ahead of the 2027 elections, adding that the Labour Party would not allow the public to be misled. The party commended the Abia State Signages and Advertising Agency (ABSSAA) for removing the billboard, stressing that public communication materials must comply with relevant regulatory requirements. Iroegbu also disclosed that the party had a substantive senatorial candidate for Abia North, Chief David Onuoha Bourdex. He said the party would not allow what it described as misleading political narratives to confuse its supporters across Arochukwu, Bende, Isuikwuato, Ohafia and Umunneochi local government areas. item.title: PSC appoints CP Usman Adamu Zamfara Police Commissioner
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the posting of CP Usman Sheikh Adamu as the new Commissioner of Police for Zamfara State. The deployment was approved following an interview session at the commission’s corporate headquarters in Jabi, Abuja, presided over by a board member, Justice Paul Adamu Galumje (JSC, rtd), on behalf of the Chairman, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (rtd). In a statement by the commission’s spokesperson, Torty Njoku, the PSC said the new commissioner was charged to demonstrate professionalism and neutrality in the discharge of his duties, particularly as the country prepares for the 2027 general elections. According to the statement, Adamu was also tasked with addressing the security challenges confronting Zamfara State and prioritising public safety. Before his new appointment, Adamu served as Area Commander, Jos Metro, Plateau State Command; Area Commander in Yobe State; Deputy Commissioner of Police, Criminal Investigation Department (CID), Plateau State; and Commissioner of Police, SERVICOM, at the Force Headquarters, Abuja. An alumnus of the University of Maiduguri, where he obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Linguistics, Adamu joined the Nigeria Police Force on June 10, 1994, as a Cadet Assistant Superintendent of Police. The commission said the approval had been communicated to the Inspector-General of Police through a letter signed by its Secretary, Chief Onyemuche Nnamani. item.title: US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America
item.description: The Copa America will be staged in the United States for a second successive edition in 2028 just ahead of the Los Angeles Olympics, organizers announced on Tuesday. CONMEBOL, the South American football confederation, and CONCACAF, the governing body for North America, agreed to conduct the 49th edition of the event at US venues from June 9 to July 9, 2028. The Los Angeles Olympics are scheduled for July 14-30 but the first pre-Olympic group-stage men’s soccer matches begin on July 10, only hours after the Copa final. The tournament will feature 16 teams, the 10 nations from South America plus six countries from North America that will qualify through the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup. The event was also played in the United States in 2016, the Copa America Centenario, and 2024 ahead of the USA co-hosting the World Cup earlier this year. “The CONMEBOL Copa America is much more than a tournament: it is part of our identity, our history, and the greatness of South American football,” CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez said. “In 2028, we will once again bring that passion to the United States, reaffirming our historic partnership with CONCACAF and our shared commitment to continuing to drive the growth of football across the continent.” The host cities and other details will be announced later. “We’re pleased to join forces again to bring the CONMEBOL Copa America to our region in 2028,” said CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani. “We look forward to working alongside CONMEBOL, the host venues, and other key parties to organize a first-class tournament.” The post US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ADC to Tinubu: Resign or face impeachment over Kano judgment
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked President Bola Tinubu to resign or face impeachment over allegations that he interfered in the Supreme Court’s 2023 Kano governorship election judgment in exchange for Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s defection to the All Progressives Congress (APC). The party said Yusuf’s recent BBC Hausa interview had raised serious questions about the independence of the judiciary, alleging that the President may have used his office to influence a judicial outcome for political advantage. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the allegation as a grave breach of the President’s constitutional oath and urged the National Assembly to investigate the alleged arrangement. “No conduct can be more heinous on the part of a democratically elected President than to make the administration of justice an instrument of political bargaining. No betrayal of the presidential oath can be more profound than to pervert the cause of justice in pursuit of personal political advantage,” the party said. The ADC said Yusuf’s account suggested that the President had secured a favourable judgment from the Supreme Court in return for the governor’s defection to the APC. “In plain language, what Governor Yusuf was has admitted to was that the President of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, got the highest court in the land to award him justice in exchange for him decamping to APC. This a very grave allegation that undermines every principle regarding the rule of law, independence of the judiciary, and, indeed, the fight against corruption,” it said. The party called on the National Assembly to initiate impeachment proceedings against Tinubu and compel all parties to the alleged arrangement to provide evidence. It warned that the alleged interference, if established, would undermine confidence in the Supreme Court and send a damaging signal to international investors about the state of the rule of law in Nigeria. “The Supreme Court is not an extension of the APC national secretariat, and the President of Nigeria is not the proprietor of the Nigerian judiciary. With this revelation, the President has signalled to the rest of the world, including investors, that the rule of law is dead in Nigeria and that the Supreme Court of Nigeria is actually pliant to the political whims of the President. What a shame,” the ADC said. The opposition party challenged the National Assembly to demonstrate whether its allegiance was to the President or the Constitution, saying its response would test its willingness to hold the President accountable. item.title: Police arrest 30-year-old man for exhuming corpse in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested a 30-year-old man, Tapro Tareza, for allegedly exhuming a corpse at Machika Cemetery in the Danko/Wasagu Local Government Area of the state. The suspect, a resident of Changu Village, Gwazawa, under Kanya District, was arrested following reports of repeated grave desecration at the cemetery. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the arrest followed a surveillance operation mounted by the police in collaboration with concerned youths in the community. According to him, on November 10, 2026, at about 7:15 p.m., shortly after the burial of a deceased person, the suspect was allegedly caught digging into the newly covered grave. Usman said vigilant youths apprehended him while he was allegedly committing the act and immediately alerted the police. He added that preliminary investigations indicated that the suspect allegedly removed items from the bodies of deceased persons. The police spokesman further said the suspect reportedly admitted involvement in previous acts of grave desecration at the same cemetery, including an earlier incident in which he allegedly removed and took away the burial shroud of a deceased person. Usman said investigations were ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incidents and ensure that the suspect faced appropriate legal action. The command commended members of the community for their vigilance and cooperation, while cautioning residents against taking the law into their own hands. It urged members of the public to promptly report suspicious activities to the police. The post Police arrest 30-year-old man for exhuming corpse in Kebbi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Reps seek safer boats, life jackets after Bayelsa boat mishap
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for the provision of safer boats, life jackets and other water safety equipment to riverine communities in Bayelsa State following a deadly boat mishap. The House also urged relevant agencies to intensify rescue operations, provide relief materials to affected communities and investigate the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by Rep. Rodney Ebikebina Ambaiowei, representing Southern Ijaw Federal Constituency, during plenary on Tuesday. Ambaiowei told the House that more than 150 people, mostly indigenes of Southern Ijaw, were involved in the accident on November 20, 2026, while travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a condolence visit. He said the boat capsized at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan, throwing its occupants into the water. According to him, rescue efforts began immediately, with the Bayelsa State Government, security personnel and other relevant agencies responding to the incident. He disclosed that, as of November 22, several people had been rescued alive with varying degrees of injuries and discomfort, while others had died. The rescued victims, he said, were taken to medical facilities in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area and government hospitals in Yenagoa for treatment, while search and rescue operations continued for missing persons and possible survivors. The lawmaker expressed concern that several victims were still missing, despite the efforts of the state government, and called for a broader search operation. He said the tragedy had plunged families and residents of Southern Ijaw, particularly Ukubie and neighbouring communities, into mourning. Ambaiowei attributed the vulnerability of riverine communities partly to the poor condition of boats used for transportation, noting that many were old, overworked and overloaded because of the scarcity of vessels. He also lamented the absence of life jackets, floaters and other water safety equipment, as well as inadequate enforcement of their use, despite waterways being the major means of transportation in the largely riverine constituency. The lawmaker said the communities had limited access to motorable roads, despite ongoing road construction efforts by the Bayelsa State Government, leaving residents heavily dependent on waterways. He warned that failure by the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and other relevant bodies to intensify rescue operations and provide relief materials could worsen the impact of the tragedy. Ambaiowei added that the affected communities depended largely on fishing for food and income, stressing that the accident had disrupted their livelihoods and economic activities. He commended President Bola Tinubu for sending Vice-President Kashim Shettima to the affected area to sympathise with families of the deceased. item.title: Oyo 2027: ‘I won’t step down for anyone,’ ADC guber candidate vows
item.description: By Adeola Badru The African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Oyo State, Adegboyega Adegoke, has dismissed rumours that he is planning to withdraw from the 2027 governorship race, declaring that he is determined to contest and win the election. Adegoke, who described himself as a committed contender in the race, said he would not step down for any candidate under any circumstances, insisting that his ambition was driven by his determination to implement his policy agenda, tagged SOLUTIONS, for the benefit of residents of the state. The ADC candidate made his position known in a statement issued by his media team on Tuesday, in which he described the reports of his planned withdrawal as unfounded, unfortunate and misleading. He said he remained resolute in his ambition to become the next governor of Oyo State, adding that he was not in the race as a placeholder for any other candidate. “Let me state unequivocally that I am not stepping down for anybody. I am in this race to win and become the next occupier of the Agodi Governor’s Office,” Adegoke said. He added: “The rumour is unfounded, unfortunate and misleading. I have stated many times that I am not a placeholder. I am the Oyo State governorship candidate of our great party, the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the next Executive Governor of Oyo State, Insha Allah.” Adegoke said his ambition was anchored on his determination to deliver the promises contained in his SOLUTIONS agenda, which he said was designed to address the needs of the people and improve their welfare. He urged his supporters across the state to remain steadfast and not allow the rumours to distract them from the campaign, assuring them that he remained fully committed to the governorship contest. The ADC candidate attributed the speculation to individuals who, according to him, were unsettled by his growing popularity and prospects of victory at the polls. He further expressed confidence that his ambition would be realised, declaring that no individual or group could frustrate what he described as God’s plan for his emergence as the next governor of Oyo State. “Nobody can stop the plan of God to make me the next Executive Governor of Oyo State,” he said. item.title: Northern governors dissolve NNDC board, order reorganisation
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA — The 19 Northern States, which jointly own the New Nigerian Development Company (NNDC), have resolved to dissolve its Board of Directors and constitute a new one as part of efforts to reposition the company. The decision was taken by the Secretaries to the Governments of the 19 Northern States, representing their respective state governments as shareholders, at a Special General Meeting held in Kaduna on Tuesday. However, the dissolution will take effect upon the valid adoption of the relevant ordinary resolutions at a duly convened General Meeting and compliance with applicable statutory requirements. Addressing journalists after the meeting, the Secretary to the Gombe State Government, Prof. Ibrahim Abubakar Njodi, said the shareholders had resolved to undertake a comprehensive reorganisation and repositioning of the company. He said the exercise was aimed at strengthening NNDC’s institutional capacity, improving corporate governance, enhancing operational efficiency and repositioning it as a viable investment and development institution serving the collective economic interests of the 19 Northern States. Njodi disclosed that a new Board of Directors would be constituted to provide strategic leadership, effective supervision, policy direction and corporate oversight. He said the composition, nomination and appointment of the new board would reflect the ownership interests of the participating states, the provisions of the company’s Memorandum and Articles of Association, and the requirements of the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020. According to him, shareholders would subsequently approve the nominations and appointments of the new directors in accordance with the company’s constitutional documents and applicable laws. The Gombe SSG said the incoming board, upon its lawful constitution, had been directed to undertake a comprehensive review of the company’s existing management structure, personnel, administrative arrangements, operational framework and performance. He added that the new board would take appropriate measures to reorganise and strengthen the company’s management to promote accountability, professionalism and improved corporate performance, in line with its statutory and fiduciary responsibilities and applicable employment laws. Njodi further disclosed that the incoming board would conduct a comprehensive corporate governance, financial, administrative and operational audit of the company. He said the audit would examine NNDC’s financial position, assets and liabilities, existing investments, subsidiaries, joint ventures and commercial interests. It would also assess the performance and profitability of the company’s investments, compliance with statutory, regulatory and corporate governance obligations, as well as existing contractual commitments and outstanding obligations. item.title: Police Invite Omo-Agege, Delta Council Chairman, Five Others Over Attack In Ughelli
item.description: The Delta State Police Command has invited a former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Chairman Jaro Egbo and five others for questioning over the deadly attack on a campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. The police said the invitations were part of an ongoing investigation into the violence that occurred during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, on Monday. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said the invited individuals had been asked to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) at the police headquarters in Asaba on specified dates. Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, is expected to appear on Thursday at 11 a.m., while Egbo has been invited for 2 p.m. on the same day. The five other invitees are Gowon Egoide, a former chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent youth chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide; Erukaye Egoide, Egoide’s nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate of Egoide. Photo of a Nigerian Police They are expected to appear before the police on Friday, November 27, at noon. The police said the invitations were intended to establish the individuals’ level of involvement in the incident. The development comes as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, accompanied by the Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, and other heads of security agencies, visited Uduere community for an on-the-spot assessment of the attack. During the visit, the governor expressed confidence in the police command to ensure that everyone found culpable was brought to justice, irrespective of political affiliation or status. ﻿ The Commissioner of Police urged the invited individuals to honour the invitations and cooperate with investigators. He also warned that the command would not accept the presence of supporters or other persons who had not been formally invited. The police assured residents that the investigation would be thorough and impartial, adding that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The command also appealed to residents to remain calm and law-abiding as investigations continue. ﻿ Meanwhile, Omo-Agege and Egbo have traded conflicting accusations over who orchestrated the attack. The attack left six people dead, according to preliminary police reports, while several others sustained injuries. Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unhurt. item.title: CBN Retains Interest Rate At 23% As Inflation Drops To 14.06%
item.description: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, despite a further decline in the country’s inflation rate to 14.06 per cent in October 2026. The decision was taken at the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), held on Monday and Tuesday, November 23 and 24, 2026. In a communiqué issued on Tuesday and signed by the CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, the committee also retained the Standing Facilities Corridor at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR. It further maintained the Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, Merchant Banks at 16 per cent and non-Treasury Single Account (TSA) public sector deposits at 75 per cent. The committee said the decision was informed by the need to sustain the progress made in reducing inflation and keep inflation expectations under control. ﻿ It noted that headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, supported by exchange rate stability and improved transmission of monetary policy measures. However, members expressed concern over prevailing economic headwinds that could slow the pace of the decline in price pressures, maintaining that the current monetary policy stance remained appropriate. According to the CBN, headline inflation declined to 14.06 per cent in October from 14.63 per cent in September 2026. Core inflation also dropped to 10.78 per cent from 12.95 per cent, while food inflation eased to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent over the same period. The committee attributed the moderation in food inflation to lower prices of processed food and farm produce following the commencement of the harvest season. It also noted that the composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 53.2 points in October from 53.0 points in September, indicating sustained expansion in economic activities across the industrial, agricultural and services sectors. The CBN said Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.02bn as of November 17, 2026, providing cover for 10.26 months of imports of goods and services. These include the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which could sustain elevated global energy prices, as well as increased spending associated with the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities. The committee also expressed confidence that continued exchange rate stability and improved food supply would support the disinflation process. item.title: [VIDEO] 2027 Elections: Everybody Should Be Allowed To Campaign Freely, Says Obi
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called on the Federal Government and security agencies to ensure that all political parties and candidates are allowed to campaign freely ahead of the 2027 general elections, condemning the growing incidents of political violence across the country. Speaking to Channels Television after interacting with residents during a town hall meeting in Taraba State, the former Anambra State governor described the situation as unhealthy for Nigeria’s democracy. Obi was responding to questions about the reported attack on the campaign convoy of his party’s Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, and concerns over the safety of opposition politicians. ﻿ He said there was no justification for subjecting Nigerians to violence during political campaigns, stressing that the country should uphold peaceful democratic practices. Obi also urged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to allow a free, fair and credible electoral process, noting that the party already controls the government. Beyond politics, Obi said his town hall engagements were aimed at listening to Nigerians and understanding their challenges, including unemployment, overtaxation of small businesses, lack of access to funding, strikes in schools and inadequate primary healthcare. He described listening to citizens as an essential part of responsible and demand-driven leadership. item.title: ‘This Is Payback Time’, Shettima Makes Case For Tinubu Re-Election In Borno
item.description: Vice President Kashim Shettima has urged voters in the North to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, describing it as an opportunity to reciprocate the president’s past political support for the region. Shettima made the appeal while speaking at the distribution and flag-off of special intervention projects by the North-East Development Commission (NEDC) in Borno State. He recalled that Tinubu played a significant role in securing the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential ticket for former President Muhammadu Buhari ahead of the 2015 general election. According to the vice president, Tinubu deliberately moved the party’s presidential primary to Lagos and mobilised support for Buhari in the South-West, contributing to his emergence as the party’s candidate. “Those of us that were active in the political scene can bear testimony to the fact that without the efforts of President Bola Tinubu, Muhammadu Buhari couldn’t have clinched the ticket of the APC in 2014 in Lagos. “He deliberately shifted the base of the primaries to Lagos, and he worked assiduously to deliver the South-West. And one good turn always deserves another,” Shettima said. ﻿ The vice president urged the people of the North to reciprocate Tinubu’s political support by backing his re-election, declaring that the region had an opportunity to return the favour. “And for us in the North, this is payback time. I urge you, I beseech all of us here, let us use our informed judgment and make decisions that are in the best interest of our nation,” he said. Making a case for the administration’s economic policies, Shettima urged Nigerians to consider the government’s economic performance when deciding who to support in the 2027 elections. He cited a decline in headline inflation and an increase in the country’s foreign reserves, which he said had reached their highest level in 17 years. “The economy has turned the corner. Headline inflation has come down. Our foreign reserve is the highest in the past 17 years. It’s now hovering in the region of 55 billion dollars,” he said. Defending the removal of the petrol subsidy, the vice president maintained that the decision was not intended to worsen the economic hardship faced by Nigerians but to prevent the country’s economy from collapsing. “And the President has a great deal of human empathy for the Nigerian people. He withdrew the subsidy not to inflict pain on Nigerians, no. He removed the subsidy to save the Nigerian economy from collapse,” he said. item.title: NDC Boycotts IGP’s Meeting Over Alleged Attacks On Members
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has announced its decision to boycott a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, citing alleged attacks on its members and what it described as the police’s failure to protect opposition figures. The party said it no longer felt safe under the Nigeria Police Force, accusing security agencies of failing to prevent repeated attacks on its members allegedly carried out by thugs loyal to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). The NDC announced its position in a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, on Monday. It said it would not legitimise a security process that had failed to protect its members, adding that the alleged violence had become an intolerable pattern across the country. The party cited incidents in Benue, Edo, Calabar, Enugu and Delta states, including an alleged attempt by APC loyalists to prevent its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, from entering Benue State. It accused the APC-led government of turning political campaigns into battlefields, where the safety of opposition members could no longer be guaranteed. The NDC also alleged that security personnel were complicit in the violence, particularly the alleged attack on the campaign team of its Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Delta State. Omo-Agege is a chieftain of the NDC. Gunmen reportedly attacked Omo-Agege’s campaign convoy in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area. The former deputy senate president escaped unhurt, according to his media adviser, Sunny Areh. The attack initially left four campaign members dead, according to the Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation. However, the Nigeria Police Force said preliminary reports indicated that six people were killed, while several others sustained injuries. Police Speak The police, in a statement issued on Tuesday by its Force Public Relations Officer, said an investigation had been launched to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and determine the verified casualty figure. Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, directed the Delta State Commissioner of Police to conduct a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation. The police said the investigation would examine the sequence of events, identify those responsible and establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the deployment and conduct of officers at the scene. It added that any officer found to have acted negligently or breached professional standards would face disciplinary action, while anyone found culpable of criminal offences would be prosecuted. The NDC, however, accused the police of displaying bias and failing to investigate previous attacks on its members or bring those responsible to justice. item.title: Senegal Regain AFCON Title After Appeal
item.description: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. “The Court of Arbitration for Sport has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025,” CAS said in a statement. The Swiss-based sports court said Senegal’s appeal had been upheld by “a unanimous decision”, and their original 1-0 victory after extra time is reinstated. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result of the final, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless. Senegal and Morocco players line up prior the Africa Cup of Nations (CAN) final football match between Senegal and Morocco at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat on January 18, 2026. Photo by PAUL ELLIS / AFP The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations. Those state that if a team “refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered (loser) and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition”. However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on. The CAS panel therefore considered that the referee’s decision to restart the final showed that “the conditions for resuming the match had been met”, and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore “not applicable in this case”. item.title: Nigeria Urges UN To Clear 216 Outstanding Audit Queries
item.description: Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, has urged the UN management to urgently resolve 216 outstanding audit queries, stressing the need for greater accountability, transparency and compliance with established financial rules and procedures. Ibrahim made the call during deliberations of the UN General Assembly’s Fifth Committee on reports of the United Nations Board of Auditors, where he expressed concern over the number of unresolved audit issues and called for improved performance by the organisation’s management. He acknowledged that 100 audit reports had been cleared but said the 216 outstanding reports remained a significant concern that required urgent attention. Although he recognised that some of the cases might have been overtaken by events, the Nigerian diplomat urged the UN management to improve its clearance rate, which currently stands at 55 per cent. Ibrahim also emphasised the importance of timely payment of assessed contributions by member states, insisting that payments should be made according to schedule and translated into tangible benefits. On financial reporting, he stressed that the accuracy and integrity of data were fundamental to the credibility of reports presented before member states. ﻿ He said all stakeholders had a collective responsibility to safeguard the integrity of information underpinning the UN’s financial reporting. The Nigerian envoy warned that continued explanations without corresponding compliance could leave the organisation trapped in an endless cycle of justifications. He, therefore, urged UN management to prioritise adherence to established financial rules and procedures as the most effective way to address recurring audit concerns. Ibrahim also commended the cooperation between information-gathering systems and audit teams, describing their coordination as essential to improving the quality and reliability of UN reports. Meanwhile, the Fifth Committee considered the Secretary-General’s report on the estimated use of the commitment authority for 2026 and the proposed 2027 subvention to the Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia. Speaking on behalf of the Group of 77 and China, Uruguay reaffirmed the group’s support for the proposed subvention, as well as its commitment to justice and national reconciliation. The Committee subsequently concluded its general discussion, with Canada’s representative, Sophia, expected to lead informal consultations to consolidate the observations and contributions of delegations. The Committee is scheduled to reconvene on November 30, 2026. The post Nigeria Urges UN To Clear 216 Outstanding Audit Queries appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: ‎After Daily Trust story, foundation sponsors surgery for Kano teen battling facial tumour
item.description: ‎The Ihsan Scholarship Foundation, Kano, has sponsored the life-changing surgery of Salisu Sani, an 18-year-old whose struggle with a debilitating facial tumour was highlighted by Daily Trust, restoring hope to the teenager and offering him a chance to rebuild his future. ‎‎Daily Trust had reported how Salisu Sani, an indigene of Yalwa town in Tofa Local Government Area of Kano State, spent his days along Gandun Albasa Street in Kano soliciting support for a critical surgery after a massive tumour on his face left him in constant pain and threatened his eyesight. ‎‎Following the publication, a Kano-based foundation known for its humanitarian and educational interventions reached out to the teenager and took over the responsibility of his treatment. ‎The foundation, which requested anonymity, facilitated his return to the [Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital (AKTH), where medical evaluations were conducted and the much-needed surgery was successfully carried out. ‎Medical records obtained by Daily Trust showed that specialists at the hospital diagnosed the condition as Aggressive Trabecular Ossifying Fibroma, a rare fibro-osseous tumour affecting the jaw and facial bones. ‎The pathology report indicated that tissue samples removed during surgery weighed about 640 grams. ‎‎Family members expressed gratitude to the foundation, medical personnel and members of the public who showed concern after the story was published. ‎Speaking after the successful operation, Salisu Sani said the intervention had given him a new lease of life. ‎“I never imagined that help would come this fast. For years I lived with the pain and the burden of carrying this tumour on my face. Today, I feel hopeful again,” he said. ‎The teenager had earlier told Daily Trust that the illness had forced him out of school and shattered his dreams, as his family could not afford the cost of treatment. ‎In a further boost to his recovery and future, the foundation also pledged to support his long-term rehabilitation by either sponsoring his education or providing him with full startup capital to establish a business and become self-reliant. ‎‎A representative of the foundation said the decision was informed by the need to ensure that the teenager not only receives medical care but also has the opportunity to build a productive life after recovery. ‎‎“Our concern is not limited to the surgery alone. We want him to be able to stand on his own feet and pursue his dreams. Whether through formal education or entrepreneurship, we will support him to become self-reliant,” the representative said.
